title: Connection Expectations
description: The connections a node type is expected to have, one file per layer (spec/schemas/expectations/{layer}.expectations.json). An expectation is softer than a relationship schema's 'required' flag: an unmet expectation is reported as a gap when a change is planned (changeset_brief) and as a warning at most, never as a validation error. Every connection an expectation names must also be a triple the relationship catalog allows; one that no longer is (a predicate retired, a type renamed) is dropped with a warning when the spec is built, not treated as an error.

layer.description: Canonical layer id of the source types in this file, e.g. 'application', 'data-store'.

id.description: Stable id: '{source spec node id}.{kebab-case name}', e.g. 'application.applicationfunction.performed-by'.

source.description: Spec node id of the type that carries the expectation, e.g. 'application.applicationfunction'. Must be in this file's layer.

rationale.description: One line on why a reviewer would flag the connection's absence as a real omission.

anyOf.description: The expectation is met when an element has at least one of these connections.

direction.description: 'outgoing': the element is the relationship's source (element --predicate--> other). 'incoming': the element is its target (other --predicate--> element).

other.description: The other end. 'types' and 'layers' are alternatives (an element matching either counts); omit both for any type the catalog allows with this predicate.

layers.description: Canonical layer ids; any type in these layers the catalog allows with this predicate.
